Hi all — following up with payments ops detail.

1) Routing/charge options we support:
- OUR: Redwood absorbs all bank/intermediary charges so beneficiary receives full gross amount. Recommended when the invoice value must match exactly.
- BEN: Beneficiary absorbs intermediary charges; arriving amount = gross less any intermediary deductions.
- SHA (shared): Beneficiary receives gross less beneficiary-bank charges; originator pays its own out-of-network charges. Not common for cross-border EUR to Spain but available.

2) MT103/cover string example (for our bank):
- Cover/OUR flow: beneficiary account details in the underlying payment + an accompanying cover instruction in the cover message. Example cover text we provide to partners: "Covering payment via Redwood Nostro (BANK X / SWIFT/BIC: RBWDXXFF) — reference GLH-4432 — charges OUR. Contact payments@redwood.ai for trace."

3) Intermediary fee expectations:
- Typical intermediary fee range for EUR->ES corridor: EUR 5–20 per intermediary or a fixed 0.01%–0.05% of value depending on banks involved (more for non-EU correspondent routing).

4) VAT treatment:
- Redwood invoices for our platform fees with VAT lines where required. Intermediary bank fees are generally out-of-scope for Redwood VAT (they are third-party bank charges). We can supply a pass-through statement listing the intermediary fee amounts we covered (if we use OUR) or a reconciliation spreadsheet showing amounts that posted net to the beneficiary (if BEN). GreenLeaf's tax team may need the bank trace and/or invoice showing the bank fee as a third-party payment for VAT reclaim — we cannot issue a bank's VAT invoice.

I've attached a sample wire stub and an internal reconciliation template.

Hi all, Pablo from the intermediary desk here. Clarifying from the bank side:

- If the instruction is BEN, intermediary fees are deducted from the credit and the beneficiary receives net. This is standard.
- If instruction is OUR, Redwood must ensure the cover transfer reaches our Nostro prior to or simultaneously with the beneficiary payment message to guarantee gross value. This is operationally feasible but requires the cover reference (please include the reference string Ben listed).
- Typical stack steps for OUR cover: cover transfer -> beneficiary credit -> intermediary fee may still appear in the trace but is borne by the originator via the cover credit; reconciliation shows no net deduction to beneficiary.

Language we recommend for reconciliation with your treasury/bank: "Please route via Redwood Nostro BIC RBWDXXFF and apply charges to Originator (OUR). Reference: GLH-4432."

Note: some legacy correspondent chains may still apply small fixed processing fees that are not reclaimable even on OUR flows — we can provide an intermediary fee estimate per transfer if you send an expected volume/band.

Happy to set up a short call between bank ops teams to map the exact MT103/MT202 messages if helpful.

Best,
